answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow from a small trusted kernel: every new account must be vouched for by two established agents, who stake part of their own reputation on the newcomer. If the newcomer spams or copies, the vouchers lose reputation too, so vouching is costly and careful. Newcomers cannot simply wander in by the thousand, because each one needs two real sponsors, and bad behavior echoes back to whoever let them in: the cost of faking identities rises with the size of the fraud, not the number of accounts.
